bull_bear.body:
- IPO was a **pure Offer-for-Sale (₹630cr)** — no primary proceeds to the company; growth self-funded.
- FY27 capex ~₹200cr funded internally (no raise flagged); no dividend policy discussed on this first call.
- **₹166cr OCI** sits on the balance sheet as cash-flow-hedge MTM against future predictable sales — will net to zero / offset as physical prices move; not a P&L loss.
- Carbon-credit inventory (2.73 lakh t) is un-monetised optionality on the balance sheet.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Thin margins** (5.2% EBITDA / 2.6% PAT) — small conversion spread; profitability hinges on volume + hedging discipline.
- **Scrap-import restrictions** (imports ~⅔ of scrap): UAE 4-month export ban (CMR doesn't buy from UAE); **EU** threatening a ban on scrap export to non-OECD countries **from ~May-2027** and a **15% export duty from Sep-2026**; US mulling restrictions (has 50% Al import duty). Mgmt view: India has **applied for an EU exemption**; complex/hard-to-process scrap ("needs human intervention") will keep flowing to India; duties partly borne by suppliers, partly passed to customers. Multi-continent sourcing = mitigant.
- **Aluminium price volatility** (post Iran-US war spike) — managed via hedging + monthly pass-through, but a persistent risk to the P&L via OCI.
- **Absolute-volume disclosure discrepancy** (see §2) — verify next quarter.
- **Value-added ramp execution** — wrought/non-ferrous mix-up and new-plant commissioning must land to lift ₹/ton.
- **No committed margin/EPS guidance** — mgmt declined to quantify EBITDA/ton improvement.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Founder-led (Mohan Agarwal, 40 yrs in aluminium recycling; father Chairman Emeritus; two sons in the business) yet "owner-run + professional" with a CXO layer. Confident, detailed, **transparent on the commodity-margin reality** (pushed back firmly on the "take EBITDA to 7%" framing, insisting on ₹/ton), and candid on hedging mechanics and OCI. Slightly promotional on ESG/awards (Great Place to Work, DJSI #6, EcoVadis). Handled a **skeptical analyst** (Vinayak, alleging stagnant FY22–25 volumes vs customers growing 2–3×) by asserting continuous market-share gains and share growth at Craftsman/Sunbeam. First call, so no guidance track record yet.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Read this as ₹/ton, not %** — the whole model. A 5% EBITDA business that is actually a stable ~₹11k/ton converter; the % will move with LME regardless of operations.
- **Recycler supplying a primary producer** (liquid metal to Hindalco) is the tell that secondary is structurally displacing primary — the long-run thesis, with **EPR (FY29)** the policy accelerant.
- **Liquid metal is the moat, not the ingot** — 24×7 online delivery + transport/process patents create genuine switching costs; ingots compete on quality/consistency only.
- **Carbon credits (2.73 lakh t, +70–80k/yr, un-monetised)** are a free option awaiting a marketplace.
- **Scrap-ban headlines are a recurring but manageable noise** — CMR buys the *complex* scrap others can't process, and sources from six continents; India has sought an EU carve-out.
- **IPO was pure OFS** — no fresh capital; the ~₹200cr FY27 capex is self-funded off ₹449cr EBITDA.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The June 2026 listing raised no primary capital for the company: total IPO size of Rs. 630.6 Cr comprised "an entirely Offer for Sale (OFS) of 3.29 Cr equity shares", with objectives stated as achieving listing on BSE & NSE, enhancing visibility and brand recognition, and providing liquidity to existing shareholders.
- Reinvestment is the stated use of funds: ~Rs. 200 Cr of FY27 capex guidance across greenfield and brownfield, of which Rs. 53 Cr was deployed in Q1 FY27; positioning is described as "Capital-efficient growth through premium products, operational excellence and sustainability leadership".

business.body:
- **Aluminium (81% rev, ~80% capacity):** liquid/molten metal + alloy ingots (auto, ~45% India recycled-Al share) + wrought **green billets & sheet ingots** (first-in-country recycled wrought producer; serves construction + solar-panel/solar sectors).
- **Other non-ferrous (19% rev):** stainless steel, zinc, lead, copper, brass, magnesium (+ some non-metallics). Scrap sourced jointly, so segment EBITDA is not split out.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Liquid-metal lock-in (the core moat):** metal delivered **24×7 online, directly** to the customer's plant → the customer "is tied with us at the hip," avoids re-melt cost, no realistic switching. **Patents** on (i) safe **road transport of liquid metal** and (ii) **process control at the customer's end** — explicitly cited to "maintain our dominance in the liquid metal space."
- **Scale + cost leadership:** **4× nearest competitor** by installed capacity, **#12 in the world incl. China** (ICRA), ~**45% share** of India's automotive recycled aluminium; economies of scale + trained-manpower-driven scrap segregation = quality + cost edge.
- **JV technology access, no royalty:** three Japanese JVs (Toyota Tsusho, Nikkei MC Aluminium, Nippon Light Metal) where **CMR is majority**, partners minority, and **no royalty is payable** — technology + marketing support at no licence cost.
- **IP / process:** **8 copyrights** on SOPs; strong IT/process integration built "bit-by-bit over two decades."
- **Sourcing reach:** buys scrap "from practically all six continents" — supply-chain resilience against single-geography scrap bans.
- **ESG/proximity network:** 13 plants sited near customers (E/W/N/S); #6 world on S&P Global aluminium sustainability index; ⅓ power from solar; zero-discharge plants; EcoVadis bronze (84th percentile).

business.body:
- Claims industry leadership as India's largest non-ferrous metal recycler and market leader in secondary aluminium, and "Pioneer in recycled liquid aluminium supply with Just in time (JIT) deliveries".
- Moat framed as "Barriers to Entry": scale, technology, sourcing network and manufacturing footprint; and as "Integral Manufacturing Partner" via long qualification cycles, customised alloy development, JIT liquid aluminium delivery and strategically co-located facilities.
- Customer franchise of 350+ customers with 17-20 years of relationships, serving leading automotive OEMs and Tier-I suppliers; FY26 geographical revenue mix India 96.6% / outside India 3.4%.
- Deck states CMR is the "ONLY PLAYER to have multiple Joint Ventures with global Japanese players", qualified as "Amongst the domestic peer companies set considered in the Aluminium recycling industry".
- Structural tailwinds cited: India aluminium consumption projected to double from 5 to 10 Mn tonnes over the next decade; EPR recycled-content minimums of 10% / 20% / 25% for aluminium / copper / zinc rising by FY31; CBAM regulation opening new domestic and export customers.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [JVs] Three joint ventures with Japanese partners: CMR Nikkei India Private Limited (since 2012), CMR-Toyotsu Aluminium India Private Limited (since 2012) and CMR NLM Eco Aluminium Private Limited (since 2025, following the 2025 JV with Nippon Light Metal Co., Ltd., Japan); benefits cited are liquid aluminium supply and market-share gain via Toyota Tsusho reach, wrought alloy recycling with billet-casting technical know-how, and building a low carbon billet supply system.
- [Corporate history] 2021 Scheme of Arrangement with group companies; 2013 PE investment from Global Scrap Processors Limited; listing on both BSE and NSE completed in 2026.
- [Regulation/policy] Policy tailwinds cited include EPR recycled-content minimums by FY31, CBAM, and PM E-DRIVE, a Rs. 10,900 Cr scheme to boost EV adoption and domestic manufacturing; EV aluminium lightweighting intensity is put at ~3x that of ICE (battery casings, trays, motor covers, body structures).
- [Market sizing] India recycled aluminium market volumes given as FY25 2,164k tonnes rising to FY30F 3,715k tonnes, an 11.2% volume CAGR over FY26-30F, sourced to IMARC and ICRA Analytics.

latest_quarter.body: Commodity conversion model — **~5.2% EBITDA / 2.6% PAT, but ~₹11,000 EBITDA and ~₹5,580 PAT per ton**. Mgmt insists on **₹/ton framing** because LME/aluminium prices swing the % denominator. **Auto pricing is monthly cost-plus pass-through** — any change in aluminium price or FX passes to the customer; the customer bears price movement **day 60–90**, but CMR must **hedge its own day-1-to-day-60 exposure** ("buy day 1, sell day 100"). All positions are hedged under a "very strong risk-management policy," so LME spikes (post Iran-US war) "ideally should not affect us." Margin-improvement levers: scale/volume, technology, customer-specific new alloys, and mix-shift into wrought/non-ferrous.

outlook.body:
- **Volume growth:** FY26 grew ~25%; **expect similar ~25% in FY27**; FY28 also "a good growth year" (no number committed).
- **Capacity:** ~6.05–6.15 lakh MTPA now → **~7 lakh MTPA by FY27** (~80% aluminium / 20% non-aluminium).
- **Capex FY27:** **~₹200cr** already committed.
- **EBITDA/ton:** currently ~₹11,000+; guided to "**continuously improve**" via scale, technology and new value-added products — **declined to quantify**. Analyst floated a 7% margin target (vs 5.2%); mgmt **reframed to ₹/ton, not %**, and would not commit a number.
- **Mix:** 80:20 Al:non-Al today; could drift to **~75:25** over time as both grow (Hindustan Zinc zinc-alloy MoU is part of this).
- **End-market tailwind:** auto +12% in first 2 months of FY27 (EV cars +18%, 2-wheelers +12%); aluminium content in EVs ~**3× that of ICE**.
- **Carbon credits:** **2.73 lakh tons in stock**, accumulating **70,000–80,000 t/yr**; **no revenue recognised** (no marketplace yet) — future optionality.
- **New billet/sheet-ingot plant:** "possibility high," team evaluating site/capacity — **not yet committed**.

outlook.body:
- **Wrought (billets/sheet ingots)** — first recycled domestic producer; large customer acceptance; second plant "high" probability. Aided by **Nippon Light Metal JV** tech.
- **EV / future-mobility** — Shoolagiri (TN) plant inside an EV/future-mobility park; 3× aluminium content per EV (battery casings/trays, motor covers, extrusions/forgings, progressively bodies).
- **Non-ferrous diversification** — Hindustan Zinc **zinc-alloy MoU**; broader non-ferrous mix-up toward 75:25.
- **Primary→secondary substitution + EPR** — **EPR mandate compulsory from FY29** (recycled content starting 5–10%, rising to 60–70% in some products); products increasingly "designed for recycling." Recycling seen overtaking primary as the dominant source of new metal over time.
- **Carbon credits** — 2.73 lakh t banked, monetisable if/when a marketplace emerges.

deepdive.thesis: India's **largest aluminium recycler** (4× nearest competitor, ~45% share of India's automotive recycled aluminium, #12 in the world incl. China per ICRA) delivered FY26 revenue ₹8,640cr (+30%), EBITDA ₹449cr (+50%) and PAT ₹228cr (+47%), with a **structurally low but stable ~₹11,000/ton EBITDA** commodity model that management insists must be read per-ton, not as a %. The story is capacity + mix: 6.15→~7 lakh MTPA by FY27, two new plants (Shoolagiri EV park, 2nd Bawal) commissioning this year, and diversification beyond auto into wrought (billets/sheet ingots), beverage-can (Hindalco), and non-ferrous — riding EV-lightweighting (3× aluminium per EV) and the FY29 **EPR recycled-content mandate**. Watch: thin margins, scrap-import restriction noise, and ~₹166cr OCI mark-to-market on hedges.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward: raw-material scrap is procured both domestically and globally from around 198 suppliers across 73 countries and six continents (United States, United Kingdom, New Zealand, Australia, Europe, Africa, South Africa, Thailand, UAE, etc.), with a dedicated US sourcing presence through a wholly owned subsidiary; imports are the majority of purchases (Outside India 73.15% of raw-material and traded-goods purchases in FY25 vs India 26.85%). market_position.basis: Leading non-ferrous metal recycler in terms of installed capacity as of March 31, 2025 and highest market share in the Indian secondary aluminium market in terms of revenue from operations for Fiscal 2025 amongst peer companies (Source: ICRA Report); installed capacity around 4 times the nearest domestic competitor in recycled aluminium. Largest supplier of recycled liquid aluminium by turnover in Fiscal 2025; liquid aluminium supply limited to a select group of technically advanced players. Market share of ~42-45% in terms of volume sold in the cast alloy segment pertaining to the automotive industry for FY2025. Ranks among the largest players in the global aluminium recycling industry in terms of installed capacity as of March 31, 2025; 6th highest S&P Global CSA score among aluminium-industry companies scored by S&P Global.

opportunities: Positioned as a critical enabler of the aluminium industry's decarbonization imperative; aluminium is endlessly recyclable without loss in quality, making it ideal for sustainable industrial use (Source: ICRA Report).
Structural shift toward localized, self-sufficient regional recycling ecosystems as trade fragmentation drives regional circularity.
Increasing domestic scrap procurement to diversify raw material sourcing.
strengths: Leading recycler in the domestic aluminium recycling industry in India with significant entry barriers and positioned as a critical enabler of the aluminium industry's decarbonization imperative; installed capacity around 4 times the nearest domestic competitor as of March 31, 2025.
Leading supplier of liquid aluminium alloy, ranking as the largest supplier of recycled liquid aluminium by turnover in Fiscal 2025.
Strong and diversified supplier base for sourcing raw materials, procuring metal scrap from around 198 global suppliers across 73 countries (excluding India) spanning six continents.
Long-standing relationships with customers comprising Tier 1 companies and OEMs, many for the last ten Fiscals.
Strategic alliances through joint ventures with Toyota Tsusho Corporation (since 2012), Nikkei MC Aluminium (since 2012) and Nippon Light Metal (since 2025).

Facilities, technology, quality processes and engineering expertise, with recycling operations at 13 strategically located facilities in India and installed capacity of 6,05,850 MTPA as of June 30, 2025.
Experienced and qualified management team with a people-focused culture; Chairman and Managing Director Mohan Agarwal has over 31 years of experience in the aluminium alloys recycling industry.

Environment friendly business supported by green technologies and processes with focus on ESG, holding the 6th highest S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment (CSA) score amongst companies in the aluminium industry scored by S&P Global.
threats: Global economic slowdown weakening demand in automotive, construction and manufacturing sectors, reducing scrap generation and demand for recycled inputs.

Tariff and trade restrictions (e.g. U.S. Section 232 aluminium tariff raised to 50% on June 4, 2025; China import ban on foreign waste; retaliatory tariffs) impeding the free flow of secondary material.
Trade fragmentation and export/import restrictions reducing efficiency and specialization gained from global trade.
weaknesses: High dependence on imported metal scrap due to low domestic availability, sourcing from around 198 global suppliers across 73 countries excluding India.
Reported negative profit for the year of (8,385.57) million in Fiscal 2024 on account of an exceptional item of 12,396.27 million from non-cash goodwill impairment.
Rising leverage, with Net Debt to Equity increasing from 0.15x in Fiscal 2023 to 0.36x in Fiscal 2024 to 0.58x in Fiscal 2025.

overview.business_model: The company processes, manufactures and sells aluminium alloys (in ingot and liquid form), zinc alloy ingots and segregated furnace-ready scrap of stainless steel, copper, brass, zinc, lead and magnesium. It procures aluminium-based metal scrap (including used beverage cans) both domestically and from overseas markets across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas, and recycles it into new metal. Customers are primarily original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and Tier 1 automotive companies. Operations run through 13 strategically located recycling units in India.

concerns_observed: Structurally thin margins: EBITDA margin is only ~4.6% of revenue (Rs 30,371.7m on Rs 666,648.5 lakhs of revenue) and PAT margin was 2.32% (FY25) / -14.05% (FY24) / 1.77% (FY23); raw material consumed is 88-89% of revenue, leaving little buffer against scrap-price or forex moves.

FY2024 reported a net loss of Rs 83,855.7 lakhs driven by a Rs 123,962.7 lakhs (~Rs 1,240 cr) non-cash goodwill write-off; the strong FY25 RoNW of 31.08% is partly a function of a depleted net worth (net worth fell from Rs 223,781.7 lakhs FY23 to Rs 136,640.0 lakhs FY24 after the impairment and a Rs 2,212,682-share repurchase).

Rising leverage and weak liquidity: Net Debt/Equity climbed from 0.15x (FY23) to 0.36x (FY24) to 0.58x (FY25); total debt Rs 89,403.3 lakhs against cash of only Rs 176.8 lakhs at FY25; borrowings Rs 9,066.51m as of June 30, 2025 were 31.75% of total assets.
Negative operating cash flow of Rs 920.03m in FY25 (vs Rs 741.02m FY24 and Rs 6,108.95m FY23), with the FY25 funding gap bridged by financing inflows of Rs 3,256.02m.

Governance flags: FY2022-23 CARO qualified opinion on improperly-approved CCIIPL related-party transactions (Rs 3,929.78 lacs / Rs 2,174.60 lacs approved improperly and Rs 545.89 lacs not board-approved), plus a subsequent statutory auditor change after S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP vacated citing low audit fees offered.

Extensive related-party dealings: 116 RPT line-items across FY23-FY25 (JV sales/purchases, promoter remuneration and lease payments, loans, guarantees), and three group companies/JVs (CCIIPL, CMRC, KAPL) did not provide SEBI ICDR-required confirmations, with a SEBI exemption sought and KAPL refusing consent.
Pending insolvency exposure: Ugro Capital has initiated a Section 7 IBC corporate insolvency application (Rs 35.08m) plus arbitration, with an SLP pending before the Supreme Court.

Concentration risk: top-3 customers 22.98% and top-5 35.01% of FY25 revenue; automotive OEM/Tier-1 exposure ~77% of revenue; product mix ~78% aluminium; and heavy dependence on imported scrap (73.15% of FY25 purchases, US 47.55%) against a backdrop of tariff actions (US Section 232 aluminium tariff raised to 50%).

Pure Offer for Sale of up to 42,890,735 shares: the company receives no proceeds, so the balance sheet and leverage are unchanged by the transaction; all proceeds accrue to selling shareholders (including promoters).

strengths_observed: Market-leading scale in Indian non-ferrous (aluminium) recycling: installed capacity of 6,05,850 MTPA across 13 facilities as of June 30, 2025, stated at ~4x the nearest domestic competitor and ~42-45% volume share of the automotive cast-alloy segment for FY2025 (Source: ICRA Report).
Revenue growth resumed in FY2025: revenue from operations Rs 58,685.1m (FY23) -> Rs 59,524.4m (FY24) -> Rs 66,664.9m (FY25), a ~12% YoY rise in FY25 after a broadly flat FY24.
EBITDA expanded to Rs 30,371.7m in FY25 from Rs 21,740.4m (FY24) and Rs 20,701.4m (FY23), and reported RoNW recovered to 31.08% in FY25 (vs 8.17% FY23 and -265.9% FY24).

Strategic Japanese JV relationships (Toyota Tsusho since 2012, Nikkei MC Aluminium since 2012, Nippon Light Metal 2025 taking 20% in CMR NLM Eco) provide technology access and captive offtake; subsidiaries CMRN (74%) and CMRT (70%).

Long-tenured, sticky customer base: repeat customers were 97.40%/96.04%/91.13% of revenue in FY25/24/23, with relationships of 16-19+ years and facilities located adjacent to customer premises supplying just-in-time liquid aluminium.

Structural tailwind from decarbonisation and recycled-content demand: aluminium is infinitely recyclable, secondary metal carries a lower carbon footprint, and the company holds the 6th-highest S&P Global CSA score among aluminium-industry companies scored (Source: ICRA Report).

No promoter/shareholder share pledging disclosed as at the DRHP date, and reported peer-relative RoNW (31.08%) is at the higher end of the named listed peer set (Pondy Oxides 9.79%, Gravita 15.06%, Baheti 30.46%).

meta.thesis: India's **largest aluminium recycler** (4× nearest competitor, ~45% share of India's automotive recycled aluminium, #12 in the world incl. China per ICRA) delivered FY26 revenue ₹8,640cr (+30%), EBITDA ₹449cr (+50%) and PAT ₹228cr (+47%), with a **structurally low but stable ~₹11,000/ton EBITDA** commodity model that management insists must be read per-ton, not as a %. The story is capacity + mix: 6.15→~7 lakh MTPA by FY27, two new plants (Shoolagiri EV park, 2nd Bawal) commissioning this year, and diversification beyond auto into wrought (billets/sheet ingots), beverage-can (Hindalco), and non-ferrous — riding EV-lightweighting (3× aluminium per EV) and the FY29 **EPR recycled-content mandate**. Watch: thin margins, scrap-import restriction noise, and ~₹166cr OCI mark-to-market on hedges.
